title: Check: labels, selectors and annotations
description: Five questions on how objects find each other.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between a label and an annotation?

options.text: Labels are for selecting objects; annotations carry data nothing selects on
Annotations are only used by the scheduler

questions.explanation: Selectors match labels. Annotations hold arbitrary metadata - build ids, tool configuration, checksums - that nothing queries by.

questions.prompt: Write the command that lists Pods labelled app=web.
questions.explanation: `-l` and `--selector` are the same flag; both are accepted.

questions.prompt: A Service has `selector: app=web` but sends traffic nowhere. What is the most likely cause?

options.text: No running Pod carries the label app=web
The Service is in the wrong phase

questions.explanation: A Service is a label query. If no ready Pod matches, its EndpointSlice is empty and there is nothing to send traffic to.

questions.prompt: Which of these are driven by labels? Choose all that apply.

options.text: Which Pods a Service sends traffic to
Which node a Pod is scheduled onto, via nodeSelector
The order in which containers start inside a Pod

questions.explanation: Labels are the join key of the whole system. Container start order inside a Pod is not a label matter - that is what init containers are for.

questions.prompt: You try to change a Deployment's `spec.selector` and the API server rejects it. Why?

options.text: The Deployment must be scaled to zero first
Only the controller manager may change selectors

questions.explanation: A Deployment's selector is immutable: changing it would orphan the ReplicaSets and Pods it already owns.
